out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at the hand washing sink closest to the dish machine.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. PLEASE MAKE SURE TO ALWAYS HAVE PAPER TOWELS AVAILABLE FOR EMPLOYEES TO DRY HANDS AFTER WASHING. PIC PROVIDED PAPER TOWELS AT THE HAND SINK CLOSEST TO THE DISH MACHINE.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw shell eggs were being stored in the walk-in refrigerator above ready to eat noodles and sauces.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL RAW FOODS NEED TO BE STORED BELOW READY TO EAT FOODS TO HELP PREVENT THE POTENTIAL SPREAD OF BACTERIA. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE MOVE RAW SHELL EGGS BELOW THE READY TO EAT FOODS IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cooked fried rice(113F) and cooked beef (99F) were not holding a temperature of 135F or higher.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL HOT HOLDING FOODS NEED TO MAINTAIN A TEMP OF 135F OR HIGHER TO BE HOT HOLDING PROPERLY. PIC THREW AWAY FOODS THATS THAT WERE NOT HOT HOLDING PROPERLY.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: blanched broccoli (50F), blanched carrots (51F) and shredded cabbage in the 6DWR prep top unit where not temping at 41F or below. Diced tofu being stored on the counter top in an ice bath was also not temping properly at 56F. Orange chicken sauce was also being stored on the counter top at 47F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS DISCUSSED THAT ALL FOODS THAT ARE NOT COLD HOLDING PROPERLY AND DO NOT HIT A TEMP OF 41F OR BELOW COULD POTENTIALLY GROW BACTERIA. PIC THREW AWAY ALL FOODS NOT COLD HOLDING PROPERLY.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food, Disposition
violations.observation: Observed the following ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food being held for more than the specified time/temperature allowed: chili oil with fresh garlic from June 1st was still being stored in the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT DUE TO THE FRESH GARLIC IN THE CHILI OIL, IT MUST BE THROWN AWAY SINCE IT WAS BEING STORED LONGER THAN 7 DAYS. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE THROW AWAY CHILI OIL.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: Sushi rice at the sushi bar was not labeled with a 4 hour date mark on it.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL ITEMS THAT USE TIME AS A PUBLIC HEALTH CONTROL MUST BE LABELED WITH THE CORRECT TIME ON IT. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE THREW AWAY RICE THAT WAS NOT LABELED AND MADE A LABEL FOR FRESH RICE. 54 Restaurant (Inspection Date: 06/16/2026) Page 3 of 5

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food
violations.observation: A review of the menu with the foodservice operator indicates that there is no consumer advisory for the following food item(s) that may be served raw and/or undercooked: No consumer advisory was provided on the sushi menu.
violations.corrective_action: If an animal food such as beef, eggs, fish, lamb, milk, pork, poultry, or shellfish is served or sold raw or undercooked the permit holder shall inform consumers of the significantly increased risk of consuming such foods by way of a disclosure and reminder using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT THEIR SUSHI MENU MUST NEED A CONSUMER ADVISORY. PIC WAS ABLE TO WRITE IN THE CONSUMER ADVISORY ON THE SUSHI MENU AND WILL REPRINT ASAP.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Poison/Toxic Material, Conditions of Use
violations.observation: Pesticides labeled for residential use were observed in the facility and are being applied by the operator to control pests. Both RAID and HOME DEFENSE pest control spray were found in the dry stock area and at the sushi bar.
violations.corrective_action: Remove residential use pesticides from the facility. When necessary for pest control, chemical pesticides must be applied by a certified pesticide applicator to prevent injury and contamination. HOME USE PESTICIDES ARE NOT TO BE USED IN COMMERCIAL KITCHENS AND ARE NOT SAFE TO BE USED IN FOOD PREP AREAS. PIC THREW AWAY AT HOME PESTICIDES.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: multiple squeeze bottles around kitchen did not have a label on them.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL ITEMS TAKEN OUT OF THEIR ORIGINAL CONTAINER MUST HAVE A LABEL ON THEM. PLEASE MAKE SURE TO LABEL ALL SQUEEZE BOTTLES BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTNE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Food was being stored on both the floor of the walk-in freezer and on the floor at the sushi bar.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL FOODS MUST BE STORED AT LEAST 6 INCHES OFF THE GROUND AT ALL TIMES. PLEASE GET ALL FOODS OFF THE FLOOR BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Cloths for Spills Maintained Dry, No Other Purpose
violations.observation: Cloth rice net was observed being used in the rice cooker to help with the cooking process.
violations.corrective_action: Cloths shall not be used for any other purposes. For example, cloths shall not be placed under cutting boards to prevent the boards from sliding while in use. NO LINENS CAN BE USED BESIDES WIPING CLOTHES AND NO LINENS CAN BE USED IN THE FOOD COOKING PROCESS. PIC THREW AWAY RICE AND RICE NET LOCATED IN THE RICE.

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. PLEASE MAKE SURE TO BE STORING ALL WET SANITIZER TOWELS IN SANITIZER SOLUTION IN BETWEEN USES.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: multiple scoops without handles were being used around the facility in different food items.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PLEASE MAKE SURE TO ONLY BEING USING SCOOPS WITH HANDLES TO PREVENT CONTAMINATION. PLEASE PROVIDE SCOOPS WITH HANDLES BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: Employee was observed actively putting dirty dishes into the dishwasher and putting away clean dishes while also prepping food. Employee was switching between these tasks without washing their hands.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC WHEN EMPLOYEES NEED TO WASH THEIR HANDS, INCLUDING BETWEEN EACH DIFFERENT TASK. PIC TALKED WITH EMPLOYEE TO MAKE THEM AWARE OF WHEN TO WASH THEIR HANDS. EMPLOYEE STOPPED DOING ALL TASKS AT ONE TIME AND ONLY FOCUSED ON ONE AT A TIME.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Access to Handwashing Sink
violations.observation: The handwashing facility located to the left of the 3 vat sink is blocked with personal items such as a small backpack and charging cord, preventing access by employees for easy handwashing.
violations.corrective_action: A hand washing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use. EHS DISCUSSED WHY HAND SINKS CAN NEVER BE BLOCKED AND MUST ALWAYS BE ACCESSIBLE TO EMPLOYEES TO WASH HANDS. PIC REMOVED THE ITEMS FROM THE SINK.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: multiple raw items in the ATOSA prep cooler and the walk-in refrigerator were being stored above ready to eat foods.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THE PROPER WAY TO STORE RAW FOODS AND READY TO EAT FOODS. PIC WAS ABLE TO REARRANGE BOTH COLD HOLDING UNITS SO ALL RAW FOODS WERE BELOW READY TO EAT FOODS.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 70F, No More than 2 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours. Cooked vermicelli noodles had been left out on a counter to from 11:30am to 2:30pm. After 3 hours the noodles had only cooled to 84F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. EHS DISCUSSED PIC WITH THE CORRECT COOLING PROCEDURES FOR COOKED FOODS. PIC THREW THE NOODLES AWAY SINCE THEY DID NOT COOL PROPERLY.

violations.title: Eggs Stored at 45F or less
violations.observation: Observed an ambient air temperature above 45F in the following refrigeration unit holding raw shells eggs: two dozen raw shell eggs were being stored on a shelving unit next the to grill and in an area where the ambient temp was above 45F.
violations.corrective_action: Shell eggs that have not been treated to destroy Salmonella shall be stored in refrigerated equipment that maintains an ambient temperature of 45F or less. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC WHY EGGS NEED TO BE STORED IN AMBIET TEMPERATURE OF 45F OR BELOW IN ORDER TO NOT GROW BACTERIA AND POTENTIALLY GET SOMEONE SICK. PIC MOVED THE EGGS TO THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR TO RAPIDLY COOL.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: minced garlic in oil (52), unsalted butter (49) on cart next to grill and shredded cabbage (61) in the 6DWR prep top cooler where not cold holding properly.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL COLD FOODS NEED TO BE KEPT AT 41F OR BELOW IN ORDER TO PREVENT BACTERIA GROWTH. PIC THREW AWAY THE SHREDDED CABBAGE AND MOVED THE UNSALTED BUTER TO THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR TO RAPIDLY COOL.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: multiple items in the walk-in refrigerator did not have a date marking on them and were being stored longer than 24 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL FOODS KEPT LONGER THAN 24 HOURS. ALL SAUCES IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR HAD PROPER DATE MARKING, PIC USED THE SAME STICKERS TO DATE MARK ALL FOODS KEPT LONGER THAN 24 HOURS.

violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. 3 large containers of food were being stored in the walk- in refrigerator on the floor.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): as a prepping station for marinating chicken wings.
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC WHY MILK CRATES ARE NOT ALLOWED TO BE USED IN FACILITIES DUE TO NOT BEING ABLE TO BE PROPERLY WASHED, RINSED AND SANITIZED. PIC THREW MILK CRATES AWAY AND HAD EMPLOYEE MARINATED CHICKEN ON AT CART THAT CAN BE WASHED, RINSED AND SANITIZED.

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Hard Wood
violations.observation: A wooden spoon was being used for food preparation. The wooden spoon had also begin to splinter.
violations.corrective_action: Wood and wood wicker may not be used as a food-contact surface unless the wood is hard maple or close-grained and used for cutting boards, cutting blocks, bakers' tables, and utensils such as rolling pins, doughnut dowels, salad bowls, and chopsticks. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC WHY WOOD UTENSILS ARE NEVER ALLOWED TO BE USED IN THE FACILITY. PIC THREW AWAY THE WOODEN SPOON.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Plumbing connections under the hand washing sink to the left of the 3 vat sink piping is leaking.
violations.corrective_action: EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL SINKS NEED TO BE MAINTAINED IN GOOD REPAIR. PIC WAS ABLE TO TIGHTEN THE PIPE UNDER THE HAND WASHING SINK TO STOP THE LEAKING.
